title: The pro-etale sheaf of roots of unity
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. On the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the *sheaf of $N$-th roots of
unity* is the presheaf

$$
 \mu_{N,S}(U)=\{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times):u^N=1\}
 \qquad(U\to S\text{ weakly etale}),
$$

a subgroup of the group $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times)$ of units of the ring of
global sections of $U$, with the restriction maps of $\mathcal O^\times$ along
morphisms $V\to U$ over $S$. It is a sheaf: the functor $T\mapsto\mu_N(T)$ on all
$S$-schemes is represented by the group scheme
$\mu_{N,S}=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\mathcal O_S[T]/(T^N-1)$, and a
representable functor satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, hence
for the coarser pro-etale topology. Every group $\mu_{N,S}(U)$ is killed by $N$,
so $\mu_{N,S}$ is a sheaf of modules over the constant sheaf $(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf
Z)_S$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $N\mid N'$, the *transition map*

$$
 \mu_{N',S}\longrightarrow\mu_{N,S},\qquad u\longmapsto u^{N'/N},
$$

is a morphism of sheaves of $(\mathbf Z/N'\mathbf Z)_S$-modules; for a prime
$\ell$ and $N=\ell^r$, $N'=\ell^{r+1}$ it is $u\mapsto u^\ell$, and
$(\mu_{\ell^r,S})_{r\geq1}$ with these maps is an inverse system of sheaves.
